goldens.comment: In .topic-meta-data h5 a, the original code had color: scale-color($primary, $lightness: 30%) but was changed to dark-light-choose(scale-color($primary, $lightness: 70%), scale-color($secondary, $lightness: 30%)). The lightness for the light theme changed from 30% to 70%, which is a dramatic inversion

This change for desktop/user.css changes $primary from 30% to 50% for the light theme; most other changes preserve the original $primary value and move the complement to $secondary for dark. Consider reviewing this (also applies to a similar .name change in the mobile variant).
In topic-post.css the original code used $lightness: 70% but the replacement uses $lightness: 30% for the light theme. This makes the text significantly darker than intended.

The light theme color for `.topic-meta-data h5 a` was changed from `scale-color($primary, $lightness: 30%)` to `scale-color($primary, $lightness: 70%)`, which may unintentionally reduce contrast and affect readability. This change should be reviewed to ensure it aligns with design intentions.
In mobile/user.scss line 497, the lightness value for dark themes should be inverted to 70% instead of being changed to 50%. This change may lead to unintended visual regressions in light themes.

adjudication_records.issue_text: app/assets/stylesheets/mobile/modal.scss:102 — The light-theme branch changes the original 70% lightness to 30%, making the mobile modal length message substantially darker than before.

adjudication.rationale: The finding is accurate. Looking at the diff for app/assets/stylesheets/mobile/modal.scss line 102, the change is from `color: scale-color($primary, $lightness: 70%)` to `color: dark-light-choose(scale-color($primary, $lightness: 30%), scale-color($secondary, $lightness: 70%))`. The first argument to dark-light-choose is for light theme, and it changed from 70% lightness to 30% lightness, which would make the text significantly darker in light mode. This appears to be an inconsistency compared to other similar changes in the diff where the light-theme value typically preserves the original lightness percentage.

adjudication_records.issue_text: app/assets/stylesheets/mobile/topic-post.scss:182 — The light-theme branch changes the original 20% lightness to 50%, weakening the mobile link-card heading contrast.

adjudication.rationale: Looking at the diff for app/assets/stylesheets/mobile/topic-post.scss around line 179-182, the change is from `color: scale-color($primary, $lightness: 20%)` to `color: dark-light-choose(scale-color($primary, $lightness: 50%), scale-color($secondary, $lightness: 50%))`. The finding correctly identifies that the light-theme branch (first argument to dark-light-choose) changes from 20% lightness to 50% lightness, which would indeed reduce contrast for the h3 heading in mobile link-cards. This appears to be an inconsistency compared to other similar changes in the codebase where the original lightness values were preserved in the light-theme branch.

adjudication_records.issue_text: app/assets/stylesheets/desktop/user.scss:522 — The light-theme group member name changed from 30% to 50%, altering the light-theme color while adding dark-theme support.

adjudication.rationale: The finding is accurate. Looking at line 522 in desktop/user.scss, the diff shows the change from `color: scale-color($primary, $lightness: 30%);` to `color: dark-light-choose(scale-color($primary, $lightness: 50%), scale-color($secondary, $lightness: 50%));`. This means the light-theme value changed from 30% lightness to 50% lightness, which is a functional change to the light theme appearance, not just adding dark theme support. This appears to be an unintended side effect - the PR is about adding dark theme support, but this change also modifies the existing light theme behavior.

adjudication_records.issue_text: app/assets/stylesheets/mobile/modal.scss:102 — The light-theme arm changed from 70% to 30%, reversing the custom message-length indicator's intended light-theme shade.

adjudication.rationale: Looking at the diff for mobile/modal.scss line 102, the change is from `scale-color($primary, $lightness: 70%)` to `dark-light-choose(scale-color($primary, $lightness: 30%), scale-color($secondary, $lightness: 70%))`. The finding correctly identifies that the light-theme arm (first argument to dark-light-choose) changed from 70% lightness to 30% lightness. This is inconsistent with the pattern used throughout the rest of the diff, where light-theme values typically maintain similar lightness percentages. For example, in desktop/modal.scss line 50 and line 94, the same `.custom-message-length` selector uses 70% lightness for the light theme. This appears to be an error where the values were swapped - the light theme should likely use 70% (lighter) and dark theme 30% (darker of secondary), but instead it's reversed.

adjudication_records.issue_text: app/assets/stylesheets/mobile/topic-post.scss:182 — The light-theme star-card heading changed from 20% to 50%, so the conversion does not preserve its original light-theme color.

adjudication.rationale: Looking at the diff for app/assets/stylesheets/mobile/topic-post.scss around line 179-182, the change shows: `color: dark-light-choose(scale-color($primary, $lightness: 50%), scale-color($secondary, $lightness: 50%));` replacing what was originally `color: scale-color($primary, $lightness: 20%);`. The finding correctly identifies that the original light-theme value was 20% lightness, but the new dark-light-choose uses 50% for the light theme (first argument). This is indeed a bug where the conversion does not preserve the original light-theme color - it should have been `dark-light-choose(scale-color($primary, $lightness: 20%), scale-color($secondary, $lightness: 80%))` to maintain the original 20% lightness for light theme.

adjudication_records.issue_text: app/assets/stylesheets/common/admin/admin_base.scss:385 — No automated light/dark theme regression coverage accompanies the 30-file color conversion, so incorrect lightness mappings can ship unnoticed.

adjudication.rationale: The finding correctly identifies that this large diff changes color handling across 30+ SCSS files from simple scale-color() calls to dark-light-choose() calls for theme support, but no test files are included in the diff. This is a legitimate concern about test coverage for a significant visual change that could have regressions. However, the finding is somewhat generic - it doesn't point to a specific incorrect lightness mapping, just the general lack of automated testing. The concern is valid but the specific line citation (385) is arbitrary since the issue applies to all 100+ changes in the diff.
